name: manageJingleScript
description: Write and render jingles and songs (short music, played or sung, with sound effects) plus a timing map an animation can sync to. Start with action getGuide, then getSchema; write a score; checkScore and fix every error; then renderScore. A long score can be written to a .json file and passed as `path` instead of `score`. Only when the user asks for a song composed by YuE2: composeScore writes a melody and chords for lyrics, and the score it saves is rendered with renderScore. renderScore shows a player with the waveform, cues and beats.

action.description: What to do. The loop: getGuide (how to write a jingle) → getSchema (the exact format) → write a score → checkScore → fix every error → renderScore. listInstruments / getInstrument show the sounds. composeScore has YuE2 (an AI composer) write a melody and chords for lyrics, only when the user asks for that.

part.description: getSchema: one part only ("score" is the whole format, "instrument" a custom instrument's, "timing" the timing map's).

instrument.description: getInstrument: the instrument or sound effect's name.

path.description: checkScore, renderScore: path of a score file (.json) to read instead of passing `score` — better for long scores. Relative to the project directory, or absolute. Give `score` or `path`, not both.

fileName.description: renderScore: file stem for the outputs (default: the score file's name with `path`, otherwise "jingle"). composeScore: file stem of the score it saves (default "song"); when that name is taken it saves as "<stem>-2", "<stem>-3" …, never over an earlier score, and answers with the path it used.

format.description: renderScore: "wav" (default), "mp3" or "ogg" (MP3 and OGG need ffmpeg).

view.description: renderScore: what the player shows the user first — "waveform" (default: the sound with its cues and beats) or "notation" (sheet music with a cursor following playback, for teaching and reading music; give the score a `meter`, and `key` when it has one). checkScore: "notation" also reports what the sheet music had to round or shorten. Only where a player view shows the result.

autoplay.description: renderScore: true to start playing as soon as the player appears (once). Only where a player view shows the result.

autoplayDelay.description: renderScore with autoplay: seconds the player waits after it appears before it plays. Default: at once, or in a voice chat until you have spoken and fallen quiet. Set it when you will say more than a few words after renderScore.

notifyWhenDone.description: renderScore: true to be told when the user has heard it to the end: the player then sends you one message ("Finished playing …") and you can go on (ask a question about it, play the next exercise). Until then say no more than a few words that it is about to play. Do not wait for it where no player view is shown.

includeTiming.description: renderScore: true to get the whole timing map back (every beat, note and lyric syllable). By default only its summary comes back — tempo, duration, cues, audibleUntil, note counts — which is enough to check that cues land where intended.

style.description: composeScore: genre, instruments, voice, language and tempo for YuE2, e.g. "Japanese, bright children's TV jingle, marimba, female vocal, 120 BPM". Needs YuE2 set up on this machine (YUE2_PYTHON); its weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial; companies need a licence from its authors). Takes 20–40 s. Not repeatable: the same request composes differently on another machine, so keep the score it saves and render or edit that.

lyrics.description:
composeScore: the words, in sections YuE2 writes a melody for: "[Verse]
line
line

[Chorus]
line". One melody note per mora: to be sung (`sing`), write them in hiragana or katakana (no kanji, no English).

seed.description: composeScore: YuE2's sampling seed (default 1); another seed gives another melody.

section.description: composeScore: keep only this section of the song YuE2 plans (it plans whole songs even for one line), e.g. "chorus", "chorus_2" for the second chorus. Without it the whole song is kept; the answer lists the sections.

sing.description: composeScore: true to have NEUTRINO sing the lyrics on the melody (they must be kana).

voice.description: composeScore: the NEUTRINO voice to sing with (implies `sing`).

melody.description: composeScore: the instrument playing the melody (default "marimba"; with `sing` it doubles the voice).
